scope: Independent read-only O03-2 account/hospital worker lifecycle, session, startup/build scripts, independent O02 compatibility and public evidence review; O03-3 integration is outside this source snapshot.
conclusion: No concrete blocking defect or shutdown race was established in the reviewed O03-2 source snapshot. This is a static review, not a new runtime pass.

checks.evidence: shell/main.cpp creates separate parentless HospitalStore/AccountStore workers, moves each before thread start, and arranges finished -> deleteLater. Both stores open/use/close their own SQL connection on their worker thread.

AccountStore initialization emits empty session, ready, then explicit CLI identity is resolved in the worker. Account UI receives public unfiltered row snapshots and filters against its current session. Shell identity is fed only from AccountStore::sessionChanged; --test-session is explicitly simulation.

Failure handlers expose errors and release page busy state. Page readiness flags are not promoted by failed initialization. Existing account seeding is rejected before opening/resetting the existing account DB.

ShellViewport close delegates to frmMain close. frmMain checks pending logout and frmUserSet checks both account and hospital busy states, including hidden pages, before hospital draft discard. Automatic committed account logout updates identity without discarding unrelated hospital drafts.

After app.exec returns, main performs blocking queued close on both running workers, then quits and waits for both threads. The viewport owns and deletes pages after worker shutdown; SQL removal is not performed from the GUI thread.

checks.area: Role refresh and stale public lists
checks.evidence: AccountStore rechecks authoritative actor role inside each write transaction. Shared UI now immediately refilters displayedRows_ on sessionChanged while preserving the pending operation; empty sessions clear username/password/table caches. A post-logout load does not retain a former actor list cache.

Account succeeded signals follow DB commit. UI clears accepted input fields before post-commit reload and reports committed-but-reload-failed separately. Update/current-user deletion clears the store session on commit. Hospital UI retains committed snapshots/IDs before verification reads.

Root main.cpp retains the AccountStore and frmAccountSetting independent path and legacy signalLoginOut notification; shell-only embedding/leave functions are additive. Root wsl.sh account now parses the final explicit data-dir before its seed decision.

shell/wsl.sh uses set -Eeuo pipefail and builds successfully before running/tests. ARM script recompiles every listed source into its dedicated o03_2 build tree, waits for all bounded compile batches, links a temporary output, checks AArch64, and publishes only after success. No SSH/deployment is performed by these shell scripts.

O03-2 separates hospital and account subdirectories without moving previous module data. The shell wrapper uses a dedicated temp build/runtime root and a mktemp bootstrap file removed on process exit; runtime request paths are not pre-created by the wrapper before store path guards.

Reviewed main logs expose mode/platform/public paths/status only. Secrets are not passed as command-line argument values; store result signals and public row snapshots omit pwd. Queued UI input requests carry ephemeral entered passwords only to the worker. Evidence SELECT whitelists id/name/role/isdefault, clipboard paste is cleared, screenshots follow password clearing or capture only a modal, and the formal temporary bootstrap fixture is removed.

verification_boundary: No new build, GUI, tests or process lifecycle experiment was run by this reviewer.
No authentication database, bootstrap secret content or other credentials were read.
Results apply to the source SHA snapshot listed here; later O03-3 edits require their own review and cumulative runtime regression.
Production password authentication, generic user_powers ACL, RK/device behavior and performance are outside this static review.
